scale.title: The four destruction classes
scale.intro: The trained model locates buildings and reports the most severe observed class: no damage, slight/moderate, heavy/very heavy, or total damage.

dataset.title: Dataset and labeling
dataset.sourcesBody: The detector was trained on a four-class annotated set of post-hazard building photographs, each image carrying bounding boxes rather than a single whole-image label. Training ran for 150 epochs at 800px. The labelled set is held by the model author and its per-class composition has not been measured on this machine, so no image counts are published here — an invented breakdown would be worse than none. The earlier PHI-Net Task 5 figures that stood here described the retired three-class classifiers, not this model.
dataset.labelingBody: Every building in an image is boxed and graded independently, which is why one photograph can contain regions of different severity. The four grades map onto this scale in order: no damage, slight/moderate, heavy/very heavy, total. Because each region is graded on its own, the whole-image verdict is not a label the model produces — it is the most severe region found, chosen deliberately so an assessment errs toward caution rather than reassurance.

model.title: Model architecture
model.body: Two classifiers are trained and selectable at prediction time. The first is ResNet50 with ImageNet transfer learning, taking 224×224 input with Caffe-style preprocessing (BGR channel order, ImageNet mean subtraction, no standard-deviation division). The second is a YOLO11 nano classifier trained on the same three-class split for comparison.
model.frameworkNote: The two models run on different frameworks — TensorFlow and PyTorch — behind one predict() interface, so the app never knows which is active. A third slot is registered and waiting for a further model.
model.mockNote: A deterministic mock backend remains available for environments without the model weights installed, so the demo still runs anywhere. It is labeled as the mock in the model picker and never impersonates a trained model.

metrics.title: Evaluation metrics
metrics.intro: Measured on the validation split held out from the detector's own 150-epoch training run, and read from the checkpoint that ships.
metrics.detectionNote: These are detection metrics, not classification accuracy. The model locates each damaged region and labels it, so it is scored by mean average precision — the overlap between predicted and true regions, averaged across IoU thresholds. A percentage here is not comparable to the top-1 accuracy of an image classifier: mAP is a stricter measure, because a prediction must be both correctly classified and correctly located to count.

gradcam.title: Explainability: where the model looked
gradcam.body: A Grad-CAM heatmap highlights the pixels that most influenced a verdict, turning a bare class label into something an engineer can check. It is not implemented yet: the trained classifiers currently return no heatmap, so the analyze page shows none rather than displaying an explanation no model produced.
gradcam.tryNote: It is a planned addition on the ResNet backend. Until it lands, the <link>analyze page</link> reports the class probabilities alone.
